content: The American Thoracic Society (ATS) was founded in 1905 as an independent, international, educational, and scientific organization. It serves a global membership of 18,000 professionals who are dedicated to advancing the fields of respiratory and critical care medicine. The Society's mission is to combat respiratory diseases by promoting research, education, patient care, and advocacy, with the ultimate goal of reducing the morbidity and mortality associated with these conditions. History In 1905, the organization was originally established as the American Sanatorium Association, a division of the American Lung Association, with a focus on the prevention, control, and treatment of tuberculosis. In 1938, the American Sanatorium Association was renamed the American Trudeau Society in honor of Dr. Edward Livingston Trudeau, a pioneer in tuberculosis treatment. In 1960, the American Trudeau Society adopted its current name, the American Thoracic Society. In 2000, the ATS became an independent entity, separating from the American Lung Association. Mission Statement The ATS is a non-profit, international professional society focused on respiratory, critical care, and sleep medicine. Its mission is to prevent and treat respiratory diseases through research, education, patient care, and advocacy. The Society's long-term objective is to reduce the burden of respiratory, critical care, and sleep disorders, as well as life-threatening acute illnesses, across all age groups. To achieve these goals, the ATS collaborates with national and international organizations that share similar objectives. Research The ATS promotes high-quality research to advance the discovery of new knowledge in respiratory and critical care medicine. It collaborates with other organizations to advocate for research funding and priorities. The Society coordinates, develops, and manages research and training grant programs in partnership with other organizations. It provides guidance to agencies and organizations that fund research related to respiratory and critical care medicine. As a non-profit, tax-exempt organization, the ATS works to increase funding for research and training in these fields. Education The ATS disseminates new scientific findings through scientific meetings and peer-reviewed journals. It translates scientific discoveries into educational materials for patients. The Society develops innovative methods to educate healthcare professionals about respiratory and critical care medicine. It encourages and supports the highest standards of training for professionals in these fields. The ATS promotes excellence in research and clinical practice on a global scale. It facilitates the transfer of new and existing research findings to clinical practitioners. The Society provides expertise and information on respiratory and critical care diseases to organizations worldwide. Patient Care The ATS supports and promotes the highest standards of patient care. It evaluates the relationships between healthcare delivery, costs, and policy to improve outcomes. The Society establishes, reviews, and updates guidelines for optimal patient care. It advocates for the development and application of ethical standards in patient care. Advocacy The ATS promotes high-quality, cost-effective patient care. It advises and collaborates with government and non-government agencies on issues related to clinical practice and research. The Society participates in initiatives aimed at preventing lung diseases, promoting lung health, and improving patient care globally. Conferences The ATS holds an annual international conference every May, which attracts approximately 15,000 physicians and scientists from around the world. Past conference locations include: 2000: Toronto, Canada 2003: Seattle 2004: Orlando 2005: San Diego 2006: San Diego 2007: San Francisco Future conference locations include: 2008: Toronto, Canada 2009: San Diego 2010: New Orleans 2011: Denver Periodicals The ATS publishes several peer-reviewed journals, including: The American Journal of Respiratory and Critical Care Medicine (AJRCCM) The American Journal of Respiratory Cell and Molecular Biology (AJRCMB) The Proceedings of the American Thoracic Society (PATS)
